abai.text: Saqshy missed the start. The evening before, the square where lightning started the fire (white ring) was only in Saqshy's riskiest 38% of the country, outside the red zone (the Canadian FWI: 50%). A lightning strike leaves no trace in yesterday's data. But it knew where the fire would keep burning. On the evening of 8 June the burning square was Saqshy's top 1%, and 14 of the 29 squares that burned on 9 June were in the red zone, so crews and aircraft could be sent there first. Lightning forecasts are our next step.

importance.label: fire days here in the last year

fails: New fires are much harder. For squares with no fire in the three days before, only 43% fall in the red 10% (all fires: 69%). A lightning strike or a match leaves no trace in yesterday's data.

Some big fires come from nowhere. Of 227 square-days with 50+ detections, 52 were outside the red zone the evening before, e.g. 08 Jun 2023 near 50.8°N 80.8°E (1743 detections; it was ranked in the top 38%).
Satellites miss small and cloudy fires, and some detections are farmers burning stubble, not wildfires. Saqshy predicts what the satellite will see.
Uneven by region: it works best where fires repeat every year; see the region table.
